title: Finance Officer
description:
Finance Officer

Location: Kendal, Cumbria, LA9 6 SA
Salary: £27,236.60 pro rata per annum
Contract: Permanent
Hours: 24 hours per week
Advertising End Date: 27th November 2026

Benefits - We Are Offering:

As well as knowing that what we do is making a positive difference to people s lives, you will receive fair pay and have access to a wide range of rewards and benefits as one of our employees:
- 33 days holiday (pro rata including bank holidays) increasing with long service.
- Pension contributions into NEST Scheme.
- Opportunities to undertake qualifications related to the role.
- Private Health Care scheme funded by Oaklea.
- Free access to round the clock employee assistance program for advice and support
- Long service award scheme
- Access to foundation and bespoke training and development

The Oaklea Group comprises a registered Charity The Oaklea Trust and a CIC Right 2 Work Our mission is to support people and communities to learn, grow, and thrive, with kindness at the core of everything we do.

We're looking for a dedicated Finance Officer to join our team in Kendal.

The main focus of the role is to take ownership of the day-to-day banking and purchase ledger functions within the Finance Department, ensuring transactions are processed accurately, supplier accounts are maintained effectively, and key reconciliations are completed on time.

Following training and induction, you will manage these areas independently and become a trusted member of the finance team.

The role also has responsibility for a small number of customer accounts, including invoicing, cash allocation and credit control activities, while supporting the wider finance function.

This role would suit someone with experience in bank reconciliations, purchase ledger or accounts administration who enjoys taking ownership of processes, working accurately and building positive relationships with customers, suppliers and colleagues.

Key Responsibilities:
- Take ownership of daily banking, purchase ledger and assigned sales ledger activities, ensuring transactions are processed accurately and on time.
- Maintain accurate purchase ledger and assigned sales ledger balances, allocate cash effectively and resolve supplier and customer queries in a timely manner.
- Prepare supplier payment runs and monitor invoice approval workflows to ensure suppliers are paid in line with agreed terms.
- Assist with monthly Balance Sheet reconciliations.
- Collaborate with managers to ensure accurate document processing.
- Assist with prepayments, and intercompany transactions.
- Provide general support to the finance team and operational teams with day-to-day duties.

Skills and Experience:
- Previous experience in a similar finance role undertaking banking, purchase ledger and sales ledger tasks.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise own workload independently and meet deadlines.
- Able to manage routine finance processes independently and identify issues requiring escalation.
- Clear communication skills with both finance and non-finance colleagues
- Able to work independently and as part of a team
- Quick learner with strong analytical thinking
- Competent user of Microsoft Excel, particularly for reconciliations, data analysis and the use of formulas.
- AAT qualified, studying towards AAT, or able to demonstrate equivalent practical experience.
- An Enhanced DBS will be required for each successful candidate (Paid for by Oaklea, T&Cs apply)
- If you are looking for a fun and rewarding role then this could be the opportunity you have been waiting for.

We re looking for an enthusiastic team member who will fit into a small and busy team, have fun, make friends and to learn and develop as an individual.

Why join us
- Be part of a small, collaborative, and supportive finance team
- Work for an amazing charity that s making real change in communities
- Make a meaningful contribution while developing your finance career
- A great environment where your ideas and input are valued

If you're ready to bring your finance skills into a role with purpose, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and help us make a difference.

T&C's apply based on contract

title: Administrator
description:
About the Role

We are looking for an organised and proactive Administrator to support the day-to-day operations of our Advanced Manufacturing Centre. This role combines administration, document control and production support, helping to ensure materials, documentation and records are accurate and available when needed.

You will work closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Planning and Supply Chain teams to support the smooth running of production activities.

Working Hours: 37 hours per week
- (Mon Wed: 6:00 AM 4:00 PM 9.5 hrs/day ;
- Thu: 6:00 AM 3:00 PM 8.5 hrs/day )

Key Responsibilities
- Prepare and kit materials and components for production.
- Carry out component cleaning and preparation activities.
- Perform visual quality inspections when trained and authorised.
- Pack and prepare completed components for the next stage of production.
- Maintain accurate production, quality and batch records.
- Support SAP production orders and administration activities.
- Maintain work instructions, procedures, risk assessments and controlled documents.
- Update and manage registers, trackers and production records.
- Support stock control and consumable management activities.
- Assist with audits, reviews and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Ensure product traceability and compliance with company procedures.

What We're Looking For
- Previous administration experience.
- SAP or ERP system experience.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- Good Microsoft Office skills.
- Ability to maintain accurate records and documentation.
- Good communication skills.
- Comfortable working within a manufacturing or production environment.
- Ability to follow procedures, work instructions and safety requirements.
- Positive attitude and willingness to learn.

Desirable
- Experience within manufacturing, engineering or production environments.
- Document control or record management experience.
- Production administration experience.
- Experience supporting audits or quality processes.
- Knowledge of traceability, quality records or controlled documentation.

title: Manufacturing Administrator
description:
Manufacturing Administrator

Location: Ulverston

Contract Duration: 6 Months Initially
Working Hours: 37 Hours per Week
Pay Rate: Umbrella rate : 24.87 OR PAYE : 18.40 per hour- Inside IR35
Overtime Rate: 150%
Monday to Wednesday: 6:00 AM - 4:00 PM (9.5 hours per day)
Thursday: 6:00 AM - 3:00 PM (8.5 hours per day)

Are you highly organised with a keen eye for detail? Do you enjoy working in a hands-on manufacturing environment while supporting administration and production activities?

We are currently seeking an Manufacturing Administrator to join a leading engineering and manufacturing organisation. This is an excellent opportunity to work within an Advanced Manufacturing Centre, supporting production operations, quality processes, and manufacturing administration activities.

About the Role

As an Manufacturing Administrator, you will play a key role in supporting manufacturing operations, ensuring materials, documentation, and production records are maintained accurately and efficiently. This is a varied position combining administration, production support, and quality-focused activities within a fast-paced engineering environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Manufacturing Administrator will prepare and kit materials and components for production
- Maintain production, quality, and batch records
- Support SAP production orders and manufacturing administration
- Carry out component cleaning and preparation activities
- Perform visual quality inspections (where trained and authorised)
- Pack and prepare completed components for release
- Support stock control and consumable management
- Assist with audits, customer visits, and continuous improvement activities
- Provide general administrative and operational support to the wider manufacturing team

What We're Looking For
- Administration experience in Manufacturing or Production industry.
- Engineering or Quality Administration
- Strong administrative and organisational skills.
- Confidence using Microsoft Office applications
- Experience maintaining accurate records and documentation
- Ability to follow procedures and work instructions

Desirable Experience within

SAP or ERP systems

Document Control or Production Records Management

Quality Inspection or Quality Systems

Manufacturing, Engineering, or Production environments

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity to join an innovative manufacturing environment where you will gain exposure to advanced production processes while playing a key role in supporting operational efficiency, quality, and compliance. You'll work as part of a collaborative team with opportunities to develop your skills in both manufacturing and administration.

Interested? Apply now or contact me directly for a confidential discussion.

This vacancy is being advertised by Belcan.

title: Receptionist/Admin Support
description:
Admin/Receptionist - Temporary Position

Our client, an academy school located in Walney, Barrow, is seeking a dynamic and friendly Admin/Receptionist to join their team for a 6-month temporary position. This role will cover a long-term absence and is perfect for someone eager to contribute to the educational environment.

Key Details:
- Contract Length: 6 months
- Working Hours: Full-time, 8am to 4pm (Fridays 8am to 3:30pm)
- Hourly Rate: 13.70

Role Overview:
The successful candidate will play a crucial role in ensuring the smooth operation of the school office by providing excellent administrative support and reception duties.

Responsibilities Include:
- Welcoming visitors with a warm and professional demeanour
- Answering telephone calls and directing inquiries appropriately
- Supporting the day-to-day running of the office
- Assisting with general administrative tasks as required

Ideal Candidate:
Our client is looking for individuals who are comfortable in a school environment and possess:
- Previous reception or administrative experience
- Strong communication skills
- A positive attitude and a commitment to providing exceptional service

Requirements:
- An Enhanced DBS check, completed within the last 2 years or on the update service, is mandatory.

This is a fantastic opportunity to make a meaningful impact in a vibrant educational setting while gaining valuable experience. If you are a proactive and cheerful individual ready to support the school community, this position could be perfect for you!

To apply for this exciting opportunity and to learn more, please submit your application today!

title: Supply Chain Coordinator
description:
We are looking for a Supply Chain Coordinator with SAP experience to support shipping and supply chain activities. You will be responsible for preparing delivery documentation, coordinating shipments, updating SAP records, and working closely with internal teams, customers, and freight forwarders to ensure the smooth movement of goods.

Key Responsibilities

Create delivery notes, commercial invoices, and shipping documentation.

Process and maintain logistics data in SAP.

Coordinate with Warehouse, Quality, Logistics, and Project teams.

Track shipments and ensure timely deliveries.

Liaise with customers and freight forwarders.

Maintain accurate logistics records and reports.

Requirements

Previous experience in logistics, supply chain, or shipping administration.

Strong SAP knowledge.

Experience with shipping documentation and delivery paperwork.

Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.

Strong communication and organisational skills.

Desirable Experience in manufacturing, import and export processes, or knowledge of Incoterms
